reply_text:
I found one dated AI prediction from Yann LeCun in 2020, in a short essay under his own byline. So this isn't a quiet year, but it's a thin one.

- **The prediction:** in an essay for DeepLearning.AI's newsletter The Batch, LeCun wrote "In 2020, I expect self-supervised methods to learn features of video and images." He closed with "That would make the coming year a very exciting time in AI."
- **Check the date:** the page's metadata and tag both say 1 January 2020. That was the start of the year he was forecasting, so the issue may have gone out around New Year. If your rule is strict about the day it was written, confirm the date in the newsletter archive.
- **Nothing else qualified.** His ICLR 2020 session, as reported by VentureBeat, has no dated forecast; there he said "AGI does not exist". A March 2020 printed interview with ActuIA (in French) has only a vague span: getting machines to build predictive models of the world is "le défi des prochaines années ou décennies" ("the challenge of the coming years or decades"). That isn't a date and isn't about when AGI arrives, so I left it out.
- **Not checked:** the Hacker News page carrying his October 2020 Facebook post on GPT-3 didn't open (too many requests), so I don't quote it. The coverage I saw suggests it's criticism, not a forecast. The TED page for his July 2020 interview with Chris Anderson had no transcript, so that interview is unchecked.
- **Calls used:** 9 of 12 searches and 5 of 6 page openings; the first fixed search ran once even though my code crashed before printing its results.
